sections.label: Singapore legal services exports value
sections.summary: In 2020, Singapore's legal services exports exceeded $0.9 billion, over 40% of the sector's value-added.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2020, Singapore’s exports of legal services exceeded $0.9 billion, which is more than 40% of the value-added (VA) of Singapore’s legal services.

sections.label: Bill amendments for legal hub
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments introduce conditional fee agreements in prescribed proceedings and refine foreign lawyer representation in the SICC.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments in this Bill are part of these ongoing efforts to further buttress and enhance our offering and our position as a legal hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There are two key sets of amendments in this Bill: first, to introduce a framework for allowing a conditional fee agreement (CFA) in prescribed categories of proceedings; and second, to refine the scope of representation of foreign lawyers in the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC).

sections.label: Third-party funding framework 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, a legislative framework was introduced to allow third-party funding in international arbitration proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2017, we introduced a legislative framework to allow TPF in international arbitration proceedings.

sections.label: CFAs level playing field
sections.summary: The proposed CFA framework helps level the playing field for Singapore lawyers against foreign lawyers in certain practice areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The proposed framework for CFAs in this Bill, therefore, helps to level the playing field for our Singapore lawyers in certain practice areas vis-à-vis foreign lawyers in these other jurisdictions.

sections.label: CFA proceedings and measured approach
sections.summary: CFAs would cover arbitration, certain SICC proceedings, and related Court and mediation proceedings, starting cautiously with commercially sophisticated litigants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, international and domestic arbitration proceedings; second, certain proceedings in the SICC; and third, related Court and mediation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As CFAs are a new development in Singapore, we are taking an incremental and measured approach, more cautious at the start, starting with proceedings where litigants tend to be more commercially sophisticated.

sections.label: CFA writing and payment rules
sections.summary: A CFA must be in writing, signed by the client, and must not pay remuneration and costs as a proportion of the amount recovered.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the CFA must be in writing and signed by the client.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, it must not provide for the remuneration and costs to be payable as a proportion of the amount recovered by the client.

sections.label: Uplift fees and legal costs
sections.summary: Section 115C provides that uplift fees triggered by a CFA condition are not recoverable as part of party-and-party costs from the opposing party.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, section 115C provides that uplift fees will not be recoverable as part of legal costs from the opposing party, that means the uplifted fees that are triggered or payable as a result of a fulfilment of the condition in the CFA will not be recoverable as part of party-and-party costs, should the client be successful in the proceedings.

sections.label: Restructuring applications in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020 alone, there were more than 100 restructuring-related applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As an indicator, Sir, in 2020 alone, there were more than 100 restructuring–related applications.

sections.label: Foreign lawyer submission restrictions
sections.summary: A fully registered foreign lawyer may submit in prescribed proceedings only with Court permission and not on matters of Singapore law.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, a foreign lawyer with full registration may submit on matters in the prescribed proceedings, subject to the following restrictions: one, the foreign lawyer will only be allowed to submit on matters with permission granted by the Court; and two, the foreign lawyer will not be permitted to make a submission on a matter of Singapore law.

sections.label: Amendment on preliminary proceedings
sections.summary: An amendment at Committee stage clarifies that a fully registered foreign lawyer may appear and plead in proceedings preliminary to prescribed relevant proceedings and relevant appeals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I would like to highlight that I am also moving an amendment to the Bill, at the Committee stage, to clarify that a foreign lawyer with full registration will be able to appear and plead, subject to the restrictions proposed by clause 2 of this Bill, in proceedings preliminary to the prescribed relevant proceedings and relevant appeals.

sections.label: Conditional fee agreements support
sections.summary: The amendments allow conditional fee agreements, providing litigation funding that can enhance access to justice and level the playing field with other dispute resolution hubs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Adjustments must be made regularly to ensure that our country remains a trusted dispute resolution hub of choice, business-friendly and thick with legal talent and expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is in this context that I welcome and support the proposed amendments to the Bill to allow lawyers to charge their fees on the basis of whether they have secured a good outcome for their clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These agreements, known as conditional fee agreements (CFAs) will have the effect of providing a litigation funding arrangement for businesses and individuals who may otherwise be unable to commence action owing to lack of funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This in turn can have the effect of enhancing access to justice in Singapore and also level the playing field vis-a-vis other dispute resolution hubs, and this is also the point that the hon Minister made.

sections.label: Court powers over CFAs
sections.summary: A principled approach is needed to distinguish fair uplift from profiteering, and the High Court may enforce, reopen or order repayment under a CFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In these kinds of cases, it is not just a simple matter of "willing buyer, willing seller".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: There must be a principled approach to determining the line between the uplift being viewed as a fair reward or unbridled profiteering that brings the profession to disrepute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also note that under the proposed section 115D(4) of the Act, the High Court is given the power to enforce a CFA in any manner that the Court thinks fit, even if the technical requirements of the CFA are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 115D(7) of the Act, the High Court has the power to reopen the CFA and even order repayment of fees within a 12-month period after payment has been made under the CFA.

sections.label: CFA access to justice benefits
sections.summary: CFAs enhance access to justice by funding meritorious claims and level the playing field for Singapore lawyers in international arbitration and SICC proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: One of the key principles which I agree with is that CFAs help enhance access to justice by providing business or individuals with additional funding to pursue meritorious claims, which they may otherwise not pursue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Another advantage is that it levels the playing field for Singapore lawyers in areas, such as international arbitration or SICC proceedings, where the counterparts in the other countries may have access to such types of funding.

sections.label: Lawyer duty and safeguards
sections.summary: A lawyer's duty to the Court takes precedence over duty to client, and the Member asks what safeguards prevent a lawyer with vested interest from subverting justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: A lawyer as a paramount duty to the Court as an officer of the Court and this duty takes precedence over the lawyer's duty to his client.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister, what are the safeguards to prevent a lawyer from subverting the course of justice if he has a vested interest in the outcome of the legal proceedings?

sections.label: Uplift fee overcharging and CFA coverage
sections.summary: The Member asks when uplift fees would be subject to overcharging charges and notes the Bill establishes a single CFA framework for arbitration, SICC and related proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Under what circumstances would the uplift fee be subject to a charge for overcharging made against the lawyer?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I hope that the Minister can clarify my concerns because the Court does sometimes look to the debates in Parliament to understand the intent of the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first point is about the coverage of the Bill’s CFA framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will establish a single framework for CFAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For a start, it appears that CFAs will be permitted for international and domestic arbitration proceedings, proceedings before the Singapore International Commercial Court, and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sections.label: Ministry indicated CFA coverage
sections.summary: The Ministry has indicated CFAs will be allowed, as a start, to international and domestic arbitration, certain SICC proceedings, and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry has indicated that CFAs will be allowed, as a start, to international and domestic arbitration, certain proceedings in SICC, and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sections.label: CFAs increase access to justice
sections.summary: CFAs will increase access to justice for litigants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: CFAs will increase access to justice for litigants.

sections.label: Restriction on uplift fee percentage
sections.summary: The Bill restricts the uplift or contingent fee so it cannot be a percentage of the claim or damages to be recovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill itself seeks to address this by placing a restriction that the uplift or contingent fee cannot be a percentage of the claim or damages to be recovered.

sections.label: Finetuning uplift fee cap
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider finetuning the cap using proportionality, such as a 50% maximum uplift cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, would the Ministry also consider in the future to finetune the cap in the principles of proportionality, for example, a 50% maximum cap of uplift from the agreed fee.

sections.label: CFA safeguards and awareness
sections.summary: Asks what safeguards protect clients after CFA withdrawal or lawyer change, and suggests a public awareness campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: After a CFA has been entered into and, for instance, a client changes lawyers, or the lawyer withdraws from the case, what are the safeguards or guidelines to prevent a client being left in the lurch after having already entered into the CFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Ministry can consider a public awareness campaign to assist potential clients on the pitfalls of a CFA and what can be done in the event of a withdrawal or termination of the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Others fear that they open the floodgates of litigation of frivolous claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, one thing for certain, the calibrated approach towards CFAs as taken by the Ministry in this Bill will help cement Singapore as a leading dispute resolution hub in the world.

sections.label: CFAs comfort potential litigants
sections.summary: States that conditional fee arrangements give potential litigants comfort because lawyers' fees are contingent on winning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, conditional fee arrangements, or CFAs, will provide some comfort to potential litigants to pursue their claims as their lawyers fees will be contingent on them winning their case.

sections.label: Fee uplift based on normal fees
sections.summary: States the fee uplift must be based on the lawyer's normal fees, not damages awarded, under the LPA amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Importantly, the fee uplift must be based on lawyer’s normal fees, not the quantum of damages awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This same type of arrangement will now be allowed by the amendments to the LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As stated by the Minister, the amendments will help enhance access to justice, level the playing field for Singapore lawyers vis-à-vis other jurisdictions that already allow such arrangements and discourage lawyers from pursuing weak and frivolous claims, as they run the risk of not being paid in the event they do not win.

sections.label: AEIs offset legal costs
sections.summary: States that AEIs let litigants offset some legal costs, particularly the other party's lawyers' costs if they lose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AEIs are designed to assist litigants by allowing them to offset some of their legal costs in litigation, in particular, the costs of the other party’s lawyers if they lose their case.

sections.label: Monitoring AEIs and CFA regulations
sections.summary: Says the Ministry and MAS should monitor AEIs and consider regulations, and lists matters the Minister may prescribe for CFAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, it would also be important for the Ministry and MAS to monitor how AEIs are being offered, and whether it is necessary to introduce regulations on such insurance schemes to ensure that insurance companies do not occupy a gatekeeping position in the civil justice system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These include that the Minister may prescribe, amongst other things, the form, the terms and conditions of CFAs, the maximum limits on remuneration or costs including the uplift fee, information a solicitor must provide to a client before a CFA is entered into, and requirements as regards parties to a CFA.

sections.label: CFAs in international mediation
sections.summary: Ministry is assessing standalone international and domestic mediation proceedings as part of an ongoing study of CFAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked if CFAs would be allowed to act in international mediation proceedings that do not arise from permitted categories of arbitration or litigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: My Ministry is currently assessing standalone international and domestic mediation proceedings holistically, as part of a separate ongoing study of the CFAs.

sections.label: Mediation proceedings study assessment
sections.summary: Ministry assessed it prudent to consider standalone international and domestic mediation proceedings holistically in an ongoing CFAs study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For these reasons, to answer Mr Louis Ng's point, my Ministry has assessed that it would be prudent to consider standalone international and domestic mediation proceedings holistically, as part of an ongoing study of CFAs.

sections.label: CFAs in transferred proceedings
sections.summary: CFAs are not permitted in cases transferred from or to a forum where CFAs are not permitted, including High Court and SICC transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Generally, otherwise, CFAs are not permitted in cases which are transferred from or to a forum where CFAs are not permitted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in the particular example that Mr Louis Ng highlighted about the High Court and the SICC, for the time being, CFAs will not be permitted for proceedings that are transferred from the High Court to the SICC and vice versa.

sections.label: Solicitor-and-client costs taxation
sections.summary: Solicitor-and-client costs under a CFA are generally not subject to a taxation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Generally, Sir, solicitor-and-client costs under a CFA are not subject to a taxation.

sections.label: Client liability for cost orders
sections.summary: Under a CFA, a client remains liable for any cost orders made against the client.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under a CFA, a client will continue to be liable for any cost orders that may be made against the client.

sections.label: CFAs and frivolous litigation
sections.summary: Introduction of CFAs would, on its own, be unlikely to lead to an increase in frivolous litigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, the prospect of increased frivolous litigation and raised litigation costs from CFAs – several Members have touched upon this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We expect that the introduction of CFAs would, on its own, per se, be unlikely to lead to an increase in frivolous litigation.

sections.label: CFAs in England and Wales
sections.summary: Data from England and Wales suggests CFAs have not caused an increase in unmeritorious cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For instance, in England and Wales, data suggests that CFAs have not caused an increase in unmeritorious cases.

sections.label: Rules and safeguards against abuse
sections.summary: Rules and safeguards will be implemented to minimise abuse of CFAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As mentioned in my earlier speech, we will also be implementing rules and safeguards to minimise the abuse of CFAs.

sections.label: CFA fee arrangement requirements
sections.summary: Parties may structure CFAs freely but must meet framework requirements, including cooling off, writing, and no fee based on damages proportion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think I covered this in my initial remarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I think what we want to do is to say that we do not proscribe how parties may choose to structure the fee arrangement, their CFAs, but at the same time, have oversight by reasons set out in the framework, with requirements that they must fulfil, including the "cooling off" period, including the fact that it must be in writing, and also ensuring that parties do not agree a fee that is based on a proportion of the returns from damages or otherwise, in the case itself, which would then has no co-relation to the effort by lawyers.

sections.label: Client changing lawyers under CFA
sections.summary: Section 115F of the Bill provides for consequences when a client changes lawyers after entering a CFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Where a client changes lawyers after a CFA is entered into with the first lawyer, section 115F of the Bill contemplates this scenario and provides for the consequences of such change.

sections.label: Differentiated targeted safeguards flexibility
sections.summary: Differentiated and targeted safeguards are required, with flexibility to adjust them as the framework is monitored and refined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And hence, differentiated and targeted safeguards will be required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There will be flexibility to appropriately adjust the safeguards, as we continue to monitor and refine the framework.

sections.label: CFA framework benefits and review
sections.summary: The Ministry will review the reforms for future expansion, believing the CFA framework brings multi-faceted benefits and enhances Singapore's dispute resolution hub status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: My Ministry, as I have said, will continue to review the reforms proposed in this Bill for future expansion and what other safeguards will be necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But we believe that the introduction of a CFA framework in this form has the potential to bring multi-faceted benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It provides a further avenue for litigants to pursue meritorious claims and levels the playing field for our lawyers, particularly on the international setting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It will also signal Singapore's progressiveness and our responsiveness to the needs and realities of the industry and further enhance Singapore's status as a premier, first-class dispute resolution hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I assure Members that we will continue to stay responsive and engage in active dialogue amongst all stakeholders as we study the progress of our initial framework and look at the extent to which this might be extended to our proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I had earlier in my speech explained the reasons and the rational for making this amendment.
